correctness.rationale: Every last selected-type mark at ordinary coupon coverage is independent Bernoulli, independent of the label history; exact stationarity and independence follow. The product Markov return kernel and stationary first-hit convolution prove the finite PGF. Uniform logarithmic factor approximation and dominated convergence prove the limit, with a proper immigration–death plus finite Bernoulli-chain construction. The Gumbel component comes from classical coupon collection; exact and numerical tests passed 265 assertions.

value.rationale: The finite-defect critical law gives a structural phase distinction omitted by single-parameter loss models: collective microscopic heterogeneity is asymptotically invisible beyond total intensity, but any persistent high-loss type contributes an independent two-state obstruction. The explicit first-hitting Laplace transform and the atom-at-zero comparison provide measurable nontrivial consequences for stochastic collection reliability.
